description: User story under REQ-190 for the backstop (FBS-221). With the backstop adopted (rcf/define/backstop.json), rcf build bundle --next will not hand out a later spec while any FBS inside the window is complete and not verified; --allow-unverified records a reasoned override. A tree with no backstop.json is grandfathered.
asA: a stage-keeper dispatching the next build hand
iWant: the tool to refuse the next bundle while a merged spec is unverified
soThat: the backstop is enforced by the tool, not by whoever writes the brief

acceptanceCriteria.description: [failure] Given rcf/define/backstop.json with fromBuildOrder N and an FBS with buildOrder >= N at complete, when rcf build bundle --next runs, then it exits 4 with "backstop: <k> merged spec(s) complete and not verified: <ids>; run rcf build finalise <id> or pass --allow-unverified \"<reason>\"" and emits no bundle.

[happy] Given the same tree, when rcf build bundle --next --allow-unverified "hotfix while FBS-xxx re-verifies" runs, then the bundle is emitted, backstop.overrides in rcf/define/backstop.json gains { reason, by, at, unverifiedFbsIds } and stdout carries "backstop overridden: <reason>"; an empty reason exits 2.

[edge] Given a tree with no rcf/define/backstop.json, or one whose complete FBS all have buildOrder below fromBuildOrder, when rcf build bundle --next runs, then the backstop does not refuse and the bundle behaves as before.

[happy] Given a tree without a backstop record, when rcf build backstop adopt --from FBS-218 runs, then rcf/define/backstop.json holds { fromBuildOrder: 218, adoptedAt, adoptedBy } and the command exits 0; an unknown FBS id exits 3 and a missing --from exits 2.

title: bundle --next refuses while a merged spec is complete and not verified
